To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the mass of the exchangeable magnesium pool is closely related to body weight, 2) the rate of magnesium efflux from this exchangeable pool is closely related both to body weight and to fat-free mass, and 3) these relationships are more evident with magnesium than with calcium.
body composition is a strong predictor of magnesium kinetics and that the mass of the exchangeable magnesium pool is a strong predictor both of body composition and of magnesium efflux.
magnesium kinetics are closely related to body composition and that fat-free mass is the single most important body composition measure that correlates with magnesium kinetic parameters.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a model of magnesium and calcium metabolism in children that will permit the determination of magnesium and calcium requirements in children.
the application of stable isotope techniques to the study of magnesium and calcium metabolism and the use of these data in the development of dietary recommendations.
the development of methods to assess magnesium metabolism.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
body composition measures such magnesium mass, fat-free mass, or body weight are better predictors of magnesium kinetic data than are body calcium mass or lean body mass.
the magnesium exchangeable body pool is closely related to the body composition of fat-free mass.
magnesium kinetic data are related to body composition, particularly fat-free mass, in healthy children.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the magnesium exchangeable pools are closely related to body weight, and that this relationship is more apparent than with calcium.
the magnesium exchangeable body pool is related to fat-free mass, and that the efflux rate from this pool is related to body weight, but the relationship with fat-free mass is not as strong.
magnesium kinetics and body composition measures are closely related in healthy children.
The main takeaway from our work is that
magnesium kinetics and body composition are closely related.
body composition, and especially fat-free mass, is a key determinant of magnesium kinetics and that magnesium kinetics may be used to assess body composition.
magnesium kinetic data are closely linked to body weight and, to a lesser extent, to body composition.
